newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen under pressure after sharp rise.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen under pressure after sharp rise.

text.p: Shares are expected to see some selling pressure on Friday, after rising sharply on Thursday on rumours of boosting measures, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 14.30 points, or 1.98 percent, to a close of 736.92.

"We have to look at yesterday's climb as a technical rebound, due to the cheapness of most stocks and also talk the government would boost the market," said Lee Sang-koo, a Hyundai Securities market analyst. "It's very possibe that some profit-taking will emerge."
However, brokers said that a decline in market interest rates would help support the index from falling sharply.
Three-year corporate bonds closed Thursday at 12.22 percent, down from Wednesday's 12.33 percent.

They said that there were rumours circulating the market that, among other measures, the government would allow pension funds to increase their investment in the bourse, by as much as a total of 800 billion won. The finance ministry has said it does not comment on market rumours.
